record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Can K-stability be applied to chiral rings in dimensions other than four, such as settings related to F-theorem or c-theorem, and can K-stability accommodate accidental symmetries that emerge along renormalization-group flow?

evidence.quote: Question 17. Can we also apply K-stability to chiral rings in other dimensions? Can K-stability cope with accidental symmetries that might appear under RG flow?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In four-dimensional N=1 superconformal field theories, the chiral ring (the ring of holomorphic gauge-invariant operators modulo F-term relations) of a theory dual to a Calabi–Yau cone singularity is known to be "stable" precisely when the cone admits a Ricci-flat Kähler conic metric; equivalently, the affine variety Spec of the chiral ring is K-stable as a Fano cone singularity, and the superconformal R-charge is recovered by volume minimization (the geometric counterpart of a-maximization).

(a) Develop an analogous K-stability framework for chiral rings of superconformal theories in dimensions other than four. Concretely, formulate and prove a K-stability criterion whose associated extremization principle reproduces:
  (i) the F-maximization principle that determines the superconformal R-symmetry of three-dimensional N=2 superconformal field theories (relevant for the F-theorem); and
  (ii) the c-extremization principle that determines the superconformal R-symmetry of two-dimensional N=(0,2) superconformal field theories (relevant for the c-theorem).
State the precise notion of test configuration, Donaldson–Futaki–type invariant, and the geometric objects (e.g. Sasaki–Einstein-type metrics on links of cone singularities) whose existence is equivalent to this stability.

(b) Extend the K-stability framework so that it accounts for accidental symmetries that emerge along the renormalization-group flow — i.e. U(1) symmetries which act trivially on the UV theory but mix with the superconformal R-symmetry at the infrared fixed point, so that certain chiral operators hit the unitarity bound and decouple. Determine how the set of test configurations and the extremization functional must be modified so that the stable point correctly predicts the IR superconformal R-charge in the presence of such accidental symmetries.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that the equivalence between K-stability of three-dimensional Fano cone singularities and stability of chiral rings of 4d N=1 SCFTs is established, but extensions to other dimensions (3d F-maximization, 2d c-extremization) and a systematic treatment of accidental symmetries along RG flow have not been carried out in a general K-stability framework. Recent work (e.g., on chiral rings along RG flow in 5d N=1) continues to address related questions, but no comprehensive solution to the posed problem was found.

status_evidence.title: K stability and stability of chiral ring
status_evidence.snippet: K stability ... is equivalent to the stability of chiral ring of the corresponding field theory.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the 4d K-stability/chiral-ring equivalence that the problem seeks to generalize.

status_evidence.title: Chiral ring along the RG flow in 5d N=1
status_evidence.snippet: The resulting chiral ring is different from the mere F-term equations when considering RG flow.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies chiral ring behavior under RG flow but does not provide a general K-stability framework handling accidental symmetries.
